title: A hello to nobody
step: Level 3, rung 6 — standing in the doorway
note: Used three times. Collides with door-stay-03-conversation, and the difference is posture: this is STANDING SQUARE in the doorway for a quick hello; that one is leaning on the door, hip cocked, hand in a pocket, settled in for half a minute.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. Only one thing changes from the previous rung: the front door is now open wide enough to stand in, and the handler stands squarely in the doorway with her weight even on both feet, upright, facing out onto an empty porch and speaking to nobody — mouth slightly open mid-word, one hand lifted in a small brief wave. She is NOT leaning on the door, not resting a shoulder against the frame, and not slouching: she is standing straight, as if this will take five seconds. The porch beyond is empty — pale daylight and flat spruce foliage, no visitor, nobody there. Lucy holds her down on the bed.
mustBeTrue: the handler stands square and upright in the open doorway with her weight even on both feet, not leaning on the door or the frame, the porch beyond her is empty with nobody on it, and Lucy stays lying on her bed.
